info.title: ISP Customer Support Tools
info.description: Read-only diagnostic tools for an internet service provider's support agent. Use these to establish facts about a customer's account, their service area, and their physical line before offering any troubleshooting advice.

get.summary: Check whether a known network outage is currently affecting a service area
get.description: Call this FIRST whenever a customer reports slow, intermittent or missing connectivity. If an outage is active in their area, no amount of modem troubleshooting will help and the customer should be told the restore estimate instead. Requires the area code, which you can obtain from getAccountStatus.

parameters.name: area_code
parameters.description: The service area code for the customer's address, for example AREA-NORTH. Obtain this from getAccountStatus rather than asking the customer, who will not know it.

active.description: True if an outage is currently affecting this area

estimated_restore_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the expected restoration

get.summary: Look up a customer's plan, service area and billing state
get.description: Call this to establish who the customer is before any other tool. Returns the plan and its advertised speed (needed to judge whether a measured speed is actually low), the service area code (needed by getOutageStatus), and the billing status. A past_due billing status can itself be the cause of a throttled or suspended service, so always check it before blaming the hardware.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The customer's account identifier, for example ACC-1001.

plan_speed_mbps.description: The speed the customer is paying for; compare measured speed against this, not against an absolute threshold

post.summary: Run a live diagnostic against the customer's physical line and modem
post.description: Call this only after getAccountStatus and getOutageStatus have ruled out a billing problem and an area-wide outage. Returns the actual sync speed, packet loss, modem uptime and signal strength. A very low modem_uptime_hours value means the modem has recently rebooted or is rebooting in a loop, which points at hardware or power rather than the network.

account_id.description: The customer's account identifier, for example ACC-1001.
